A-r1.prompt:
Turn the attached image into ONE real photograph: an editorial interior photograph for a high-end Scandinavian design magazine. The attached image is a rough computer layout of this exact living room with the real furniture and products already in place. Keep the camera, the framing and the place, size, shape and colour of every object exactly as drawn. Photograph it all together in one natural light so nothing looks pasted: every object sits in the room's own light, with soft real contact shadows on the floor, the rug, the sofa or the wall, true materials, depth and air.

LIGHT: bright winter daylight from the tall north window on the left: soft, diffuse, clean daylight, NO direct sun, no sun patches. Soft shadows fall to the right and a little towards the camera. The window is the brightest thing in the picture. All lamps are ON, warm 2700 K, as small warm points: the pleated pendant glows over the table, the paper floor lamp glows and warms the wall and the sofa end beside it, the two travertine wall lights wash the wall gently up and down. Exposure keeps depth: clean warm-white walls with a gentle falloff away from the window, real soft shade under the sofa and the table; airy, never flat, never grey.

THE ROOM: a calm Scandinavian apartment living room. Matte warm-white mineral-paint walls with only the faintest hand movement, a simple cornice, skirting in the wall colour; wide pale white-oiled oak floorboards. On the left, a tall white-painted wooden casement window, two casements of three panes each, set in a deep 30 cm reveal with a painted wooden sill; a sheer oat linen-look curtain in soft S-folds hangs beside it from a slim black rod.

IN IT, exactly as drawn and nothing more: a natural cream braided-wool rug with fine ribs. A low straight three-seat sofa in oat cotton-linen weave, slim square track arms with softened edges, three seat and three back cushions, round tapered light-oak legs; on it a white teddy-boucle cushion, a muted sage knitted chenille cushion and a charcoal linen cushion, and an ivory cotton muslin throw with a short fringe over the right arm, falling to the rug. THE COFFEE TABLE: one thin slab of light natural oak that bends softly over both ends into two slab legs, open underneath; on it a muted sage linen runner across its left third, a small organic travertine tray with two travertine pedestal candle holders and ivory candles, and a wide speckled ivory ceramic bowl. On the wall, one tall print, a single bare winter branch in black ink on warm cream paper, in a thin light-oak frame, between two small travertine cylinder wall lights on walnut plates; lower left, a round natural raffia wall disc. Over the table, a white pleated pumpkin-shaped fabric lantern on a thin cord, whole in the frame. Right of the sofa, a tall slim white paper-cylinder floor lamp on a thin oak tripod, and a jute rope basket with two handles by the right wall. In the back-left corner, a slim olive tree in a seagrass belly basket; on the sill, a white crackle-glaze stoneware vase with a few eucalyptus stems. Foreground: left, a lounge armchair with a light oak frame and flat arms and mist-grey wool boucle cushions, cut by the frame; a charcoal felt log basket with two oak handles holding two magazines on the rug; right, a chunky knitted natural-cotton pouf cut by the frame.

CAMERA: 28 mm at 1.00 m, almost frontal to the sofa wall, level, straight verticals, f/5.6: the sofa wall sharp, the armchair and pouf slightly soft. Fine natural grain, every finish matte. A real photograph, magazine level: not a real-estate photo, not a 3D render.

DO NOT add or change anything: no extra furniture, no side table, no books, no flowers, no extra plants or lamps, no ceiling spots, no mirror, no TV, no radiator, no people, no text. The coffee table stays light natural oak, open underneath.
